checklist.name: Lookahead (highest-risk item)
evidence: SCALERS TRAIN-ONLY: fit_dl() lines 410-412 compute mu/sd from seq_tr and ymu/ysd from y_tr (the training slice), then apply them to val and test (lines 414-415, 462). ridge_lags (line 582) computes zmu/zsd from Z=panel.lag_x[lin_sl] (train slice) and applies to panel.lag_x[te]. No full-sample standardisation anywhere.

HP SELECTED PRE-OOS: select_hyperparams() (line 486) fits on the first origin's chronological validation tail. Verified numerically, not just from the docstring: oos_start = train_len + max(HORIZONS) + 10 = 3000+22+10 = 3032 (line 854), while the recorded selection_window values end at rows 3031 (h=1), 3027 (h=5) and 3010 (h=22) — each strictly before OOS, with the gap widening with h exactly as the embargo requires. Selection dates 1974-03-20 / 1974-03-14 / 1974-02-19 all precede oos_start 1974-03-22.

REFIT IS REAL (empirical answer, as briefed): primary refit_every=750 produces n_refits=18 at every horizon; ablation refit_250 (refit_every=250) produces n_refits=53 on the identical OOS row set (both n_oos=13176). A 2.9x change in origin count from a 3x change in cadence is arithmetically consistent with origins() = range(oos_start, n, refit_every) (line 480) and proves the origins loop genuinely re-fits rather than reusing one fit.

EXPLICIT LAG / TARGET-FEATURE ALIGNMENT: build_panel() back_mean() sums rv[rows - i] for i in 0..k-1 (line 183, strictly index <= t) while targets sum rv[rows + i] for i in 1..h (line 209, strictly index > t). The t -> t+1 boundary is the explicit lag; there is no shift(1) call because features and targets are built by disjoint index windows, which is a stronger construction than shifting a joined frame.

DIRECT-h-STEP EMBARGO: rolling_forecasts() line 548 sets tr_end = min(T-h+1, T), so a model forecasting from origin T trains only on rows whose h-step target ends at or before raw day row_of(T). Applied identically to linear and DL arms.
FIT/VAL PURGE: line 563-565 purges h-1 rows between fit_sl and val_sl, so early stopping never scores on targets overlapping the fitted rows'.
PER-ROW LEVEL CORRECTION: s2 is stored per row (lines 536-540) and to_level() uses each row's own origin residual variance, so no later refit's variance touches an earlier forecast.

SELFTESTS ARE MEANINGFUL, NOT VACUOUS — this was checked specifically. primary.lookahead_selftests = {"future_cannot_move_features": 40, "past_cannot_move_targets": 40, "naive_reconstruction": 40, "n_probe_rows": 40, "n_raw": 16251}. Reading lookahead_selftests() (lines 221-272): it does not assert a flag, it PERTURBS data and demands exact invariance. (a) rv[t+1:] *= 7.3 and ret[t+1:] += 0.9, then requires np.array_equal (atol=0, NOT allclose) on har_x, harl_x, lag_x and seq at row t — a genuine multiplicative+additive corruption of the entire future. (b) rv[:t+1] *= 5.1, then requires exact equality of logy and levy at row t. (c) an independent naive reconstruction re-derives har_x columns, levy and both ends of the seq window by direct slicing. All three run on 40 probe rows and RAISE AssertionError on violation rather than recording a count. Crucially, floor_positive() is applied INSIDE the perturbed rebuilds (lines 242, 253), so a data-dependent floor would surface as a violation — the test covers the exact leak that a sample-quantile floor would introduce. The counts 40/40/40 therefore mean 40 rows survived real corruption, not 40 no-ops.
FLOOR IS NOT DATA-DEPENDENT: floor_positive() (line 143) uses the module constant RV_FLOOR=1e-7, never a sample quantile, so no 2020 observation can set the floor applied to a 1963 one.

checklist.name: HAR baseline not weakened
evidence: SAME OOS ROW SET: score() (lines 612-616) builds ONE mask requiring every model in the arm to be finite, then scores all models on the identical idx. HAR, HAR-L and the DL arms cannot be evaluated on different rows by construction.
SAME LOSS: every model goes through the same qlike(actual[idx], f) call (line 626) and the same to_level() conversion (line 625).

SAME LAG CONVENTION: all models read from the same Panel built by one build_panel() call — har_x, harl_x, lag_x and seq are all indexed by the same `rows` array, and all are forecast on the same te slice.

BASELINE IS FAVOURED, NOT HANDICAPPED: line 558 gives the linear models the FULL training window (lin_sl = slice(tr_beg, tr_end)) while DL loses the validation tail plus the purge to early stopping. The asymmetry runs in the baseline's favour and is documented in the code comment at lines 554-557.

DL IS ALSO FAVOURED WHERE IT MATTERS: fit_dl() line 472 estimates resid_var from HELD-OUT validation residuals rather than in-sample, deliberately avoiding an optimistic variance that would under-inflate DL level forecasts and be punished by QLIKE. Both thumbs on the scale point away from the reported conclusion.

HAR-L EXISTS PRECISELY TO PREVENT A WEAK-BASELINE WIN and it does its job: at h=1 the apparent DL edge over plain HAR-RV (0.005502) is fully absorbed by HAR-L, leaving -0.000055. Reporting only vs HAR-RV would have been the classic weakened-baseline result; the design forecloses it.

LINEAR CONTROL CONFIRMS NO FREE LUNCH: ridge on all 22 individual lags is worse than HAR's 3 aggregates at every horizon (h1 0.3832 vs 0.3768), so the HAR restriction is not hiding a richer linear structure.

DM SIGN CONVENTION VERIFIED IN CODE: dm_hln() line 305 sets d = loss_base - loss_alt so positive favours DL, matching the README's stated convention; the HLN factor (line 310) and HAC lag h-1 (line 307) are the textbook forms, and BH-FDR (lines 331-341) is a correct monotone step-up.
A baseline that WINS is itself evidence the comparison was fair, but it was verified rather than assumed, as briefed.
